title: Ultrametric metric spaces are totally disconnected
statement: Use the universe convention of [def-weil-size-convention], with the spaces and function sets formed in the containing universe. Let $(M,d)$ be a metric space, with its metric topology, and suppose $d(x,z)\leq\max(d(x,y),d(y,z))$ for all $x,y,z\in M$. Then $M$ is totally separated: any two distinct points are separated by a subset that is both open and closed. In particular $M$ is totally disconnected: every connected subset has at most one point. No completeness, compactness, or nonemptiness assumption is made.
